correctness.rationale: For every d≥2, P=∏a_i>0, the codimension-one Jacobian gives S(U)=κ_(d−1)P/(Σ_i a_i² U_i²)^(1/2), so X=Σ b_iU_i², b_i=a_i²/P²>0. Squared Haar coordinates have Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2) law. The exact generating function Σ_k[(d/2)_k m_k/k!]z^k=∏(1−b_i z)^(−1/2) yields degree-d polynomial H=G^(−2) and the axis inversion a_i=√b_i (∏b_j)^(−1/(2(d−1))). Formal inversion to degree d is triangular and valid with repeated axes. With known P the last elementary symmetric coefficient is known and d−1 moments suffice. For pairwise distinct roots, vary the constant term of monic polynomial (or t coefficient with determinant fixed) and retain positive simple roots; the first d−1 (respectively d−2) moments remain fixed, proving the stated local sharpness including d=2. The finite verifier was independently reconstructed and run, but is not a proof for arbitrary dimension.

The geometric section Jacobian and positive-axis conversion do not change this mathematical implication. value.rationale: Ellipsoid identification from direction-free central sections is a natural inverse problem and the d/d−1 moment budgets would be useful if genuinely new. However the precise invariant here is already mechanically obtainable from the previously published all-symmetric-matrix Gaussian-ratio moment formula and determinant generating function, together with standard sectional Jacobian geometry and elementary root continuity. The known-volume refinement is only the pre-fixed determinant coefficient. The candidate adds no nonstandard ellipsoid lemma, stability/error analysis, new observation model, difficult boundary case or independently motivated unknown exact invariant beyond that established consequence. In view of explicit prior coverage this is a repackaging of known analytic machinery rather than a substantive new mathematical gap, not a rejection merely for being elementary or lacking broad downstream theory.
